ZONAL HARMONICS.
209
The system which has been actually adopted by all mathe-
maticians (including Thomson and Tait) is that in which $n-\sigma$
of the poles are made to coincide at a point which we may call
the Positive Pole of the sphere, and the remaining $\sigma$ poles are
placed at equal distances round the equator when their number
is odd, or at equal distances round one half of the equator when
their number is even.
In this case $\mu_{1}, \mu_{2}, \ldots \mu_{n-\sigma}$ are each of them equal to $\cos \theta$, which
we shall denote by $\mu$. If we also write $\nu$ for $\sin \theta, \mu_{n-\sigma+1}, \ldots \mu_{n}$
are of the form $\nu \cos (\phi-\beta)$, where $\beta$ is the azimuth of one of the
poles on the equator.
Also the value of $\lambda_{p q}$ is unity if $p$ and $q$ are both less than
$n-\sigma$, zero when one is greater and the other less than this
number, and $\cos 8 \pi / \sigma$ when both are greater, $\delta$ being an integral
number less than $\sigma$.
138.] When all the poles coincide at the pole of the sphere,
$\sigma=0$, and the harmonic is called a Zonal harmonic. As the
zonal harmonic is of great importance we shall reserve for it the
symbol $P_{n}$.
We may obtain its value either from the trigonometrical
expression (43) or more directly by differentiation, thas
$$\begin{gathered}
P_{n}=(-1)^{n} \frac{v^{n+1}}{n!} \frac{d^{n}}{d z^{n}}\left(\frac{1}{r}\right) \\
P_{n}=\frac{1.3 .5 \ldots(2 n-1)}{1.2 .3 \ldots n}\left[\mu^{n}-\frac{n(n-1)}{2 .(2 n-1)} \mu^{n-2}\right. \\
\left.+\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}{2.4 \cdot(2 n-1)(2 n-3)} \mu^{n-4}-\& \mathrm{c} .\right] \\
=\Sigma\left[(-1)^{p} \frac{(2 n-2 p)!}{2^{n} p!(n-p)!(n-2 p)!} \mu^{n-2 p}\right]
\end{gathered}$$

It is sometimes convenient to express $F_{n}$ as a homogeneous
function of $\cos \theta$ and $\sin \theta$, or, as we write them, $\mu$ and $v$,
$$\begin{aligned}
P_{n} & =\mu^{n}-\frac{n(n-1)}{2 \cdot 2} \mu^{n-2} \nu^{2}+\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}{2 \cdot 2 \cdot 4 \cdot 4} \mu^{n-4} \nu^{4}-\& \mathrm{c} . \\
& =\Sigma\left[(-1)^{p} \frac{n!}{2^{2 p}(p!)^{2}(n-2 p)!} \mu^{n-2 p},^{2 p}\right] .
\end{aligned}$$
